title: SIP - Dissection of Logme Marker in the Session ID header of the sip packet.
description:
SIP - Dissection of Logme Marker in the Session ID header of the sip packet.

Extended the existing packet-sip.c according to the RFC 8497. If the Logme is available in the sip packet, wireshark will display as "logme : Set". It can be search using "sip.session-id.logme" in the search tab.
Trace in BUG ID 16683

Hi @atul358,

As @pquantin has pointed out, this merge request has 11 commits, which makes reviewing more difficult and which would clutter up Wireshark's commit history if it were approved in its current state. In case you're not familiar with git, you can combine multiple commits into one using `git rebase -i ...` and [squashing all but the most recent commit](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Tools-Rewriting-History).

You can use `git commit --amend` to rewrite your commit message and update your commit instead of adding a new one.

You can use `git pull --rebase` to update your branch without cluttering up the commit log with "Merge branch 'X' of Y into Z" commit messages.

You can undo your change to `.gitignore` by running `git checkout HEAD~1 -- .gitignore; git commit --amend --no-edit .gitignore`, assuming you've squashed your changes down to one commit.

> which makes reviewing more difficult

You can just click on "changes" on top and that will show final Delta, also Gitlab supports merging squashed 1 commit only.
